title: Venom & Blood: Black Blood Syndicate Make Their Statement as Mayhem Monday Rocks Minneapolis
dek: The Mid Card Champion and the self-proclaimed greatest luchador alive topple Ace Authority, Malachi Knox goes 3–0 on Phoenix Jax, and a pair of debutants nearly steal the show.
heroAlt: Mayhem Monday poster with the Black Blood Syndicate, main event winners
body:
The Target Center in Minneapolis got exactly what the name on the marquee promised. Five matches, two four-and-a-half-star classics, a debut that turned heads and a main event that may have just reshaped the tag team picture. When the dust settled on Mayhem Monday, the Mid Card Champion and the self-proclaimed greatest luchador alive were standing tall, and the rest of the roster was left with plenty to think about.

Quick Results

  1. Dame Watts def. Joseph Karr
  2. Jackson Wolf def. Noah Taylor
  3. Mugen def. G
  4. Malachi Knox def. Phoenix Jax
  5. Black Blood Syndicate (El Vipero & Kairo Black) def. Ace Authority (Ace JR & Astro Ace)

Match by Match

OpenerSingles · Young Boys

Dame Wattsdef.Joseph Karr

★★★★½  4.5 / 5 fan rating · 4 votes

Nobody expected the opener to be in the running for match of the night, but nobody told Dame Watts and Joseph Karr. Both men were making their first appearance on the card, and both wrestled like they had something to prove.

Karr came out firing with the striking game he has been promising since he arrived, a Discus Big Boot and a string of Rolling Elbows that had Watts on his heels early. But Watts is a powerhouse in every sense, and once he got his hands on Karr the momentum swung for good. The Bully Buster spinebuster, a German German suplex and a thunderous Bully Bomb set the table, and The Concrete Burial finished the job.

Watts walks out 1–0 in his career. Karr walks out with a loss, but also with a match the fans rated as high as anything on the show.

I’m here to prove that people with MMA backgrounds can still hang with professional wrestlers one way or another. I want to fight, win gold, and be the best striker out of the whole damn roster.

Joseph Karr, before his debut
MidcardSingles · Young Boys

Jackson Wolfdef.Noah Taylor

★★½  2.5 / 5 fan rating · votes

Jackson Wolf keeps climbing. Noah Taylor brought the fight with Animal Instinct and a Clothesline From Hell that nearly turned his fortunes around, but Wolf weathered the storm and ended it with a kick he would later christen on the mic.

The win moves Wolf to 7–2, one of the best records in the Young Boys division, and he made it clear he thinks his call-up should be a matter of when, not if. Taylor slips to 2–3.

That kick you just saw me deliver? That’s called THE LAST CRY! And trust me, I’m far from finished. I’m gonna keep climbing these ranks until I’m standing at the very top.

Jackson Wolf, after the match
MidcardSingles · Mid Card

Mugendef.G

½  0.5 / 5 fan rating · votes

Not every match can be a classic. Mugen and the debuting G never found a rhythm, and the Minneapolis crowd let them know it. Mugen did what he needed to do, landing the knee smasher face buster and putting G away for his third win of the season.

A tough first night for G. A win is a win for Mugen, who will be looking to build on it after a rough run.

Co-Main EventSingles · Heavyweight vs. Young Boys

Malachi Knoxdef.Phoenix Jax

★★★★½  4.5 / 5 fan rating · votes

This was personal, and it showed. Phoenix Jax, the former Mid Card number one contender, has spent the week telling anyone who will listen that he is too good for the Young Boys division. Malachi Knox decided to remind him why he is there.

Jax brought the high-flying offense that made his name, landing the Jax-ecution and Redline Press and taking Knox to the limit in a back-and-forth war the fans rated 4.5 stars. But Knox was a step ahead all night, countering a springboard attempt into the Reverse STO DDT before the Diamond Destroyer and the Knox Out sealed it.

That is now three wins in three meetings for Knox over Jax. Knox improves to 12–9 this season; Jax drops to 10–11.

Main EventTag Team

El Vipero & Kairo Blackdef.Ace JR & Astro Ace

★★★  3 / 5 fan rating · votes

On paper, Black Blood Syndicate should not work. El Vipero is a fan-favourite luchador who fights for the family that took him in. Kairo Black is the cold, calculating Mid Card Champion. Somehow, in their first outing as a team, it clicked.

Ace Authority had the early edge, with Ace JR’s Death Valley Driver and Astro Ace’s Meteor Crash isolating Vipero in the wrong corner. The hot tag to Kairo changed everything. A Blackout Driver flattened Astro Ace, Vipero followed with the Spinning Cobra Hood Drop, and the Snakebite put him down for three.

Black Blood Syndicate are 1–0 as a team. Ace Authority fall to 0–1, and Ace JR, who has made no secret of wanting Kairo’s Mid Card title, now has one more reason to come after the champion.

Backstage

Black Blood Syndicate, moments after the main event

El Vipero, the two of you could not be more different. How does this partnership work?

“Different? I grew up with nothing, bouncing between homes until a family of six took me in and made me their own. Kairo knows what it means to build something from nothing too. We are not different. We are the same blood. Black blood.”

Kairo, you are the Mid Card Champion. Why take on a tag partner now?

“Because the tag titles are sitting there with nobody’s name on them. I already run the mid card. Tonight was a message: the Syndicate wants it all, and anybody who wants to stop us knows where to find me.”

Phoenix Jax can talk all he wants about who belongs where. That is three times now. At some point the results have to mean something.

Malachi Knox, leaving the arena

I lost the Mid Card belt once. I won’t lose the war. I will come back as the demon Ace and win that Mid Card belt.

Ace JR, earlier this season

The Recap

Mayhem Monday delivered where it mattered. The two best-rated matches came from opposite ends of the roster: a pair of debutants in the opener and a cross-division grudge match in the co-main. In the main event, Black Blood Syndicate made a loud first impression with the SZN World Tag Team Championship currently vacant.

Three things to watch next week:

  • The tag division: with the titles up for grabs, Black Blood Syndicate just put themselves at the front of the line.
  • Kairo Black vs. Ace JR: the Mid Card Champion has a challenger who has been circling for weeks, and tonight added fuel to the fire.
  • Jackson Wolf’s call-up case: at 7–2, the Young Boys standout is running out of people to beat.
